purpose: Allow a future AI instance to resume the Jarvis project with minimal context loss and without reopening already-settled architectural decisions.

project.name: Jarvis
project.description: A security-first local Linux AI assistant where Jarvis is the trusted controller/security layer and Google Antigravity CLI (AGY) is an untrusted reasoning backend.
development_constraints: Security-critical project; security invariants outrank convenience.
AGY is untrusted and must never be run unsandboxed.
Do not weaken, reorder, skip, or silently redesign frozen gates/invariants.
No new capability or expanded authority after a security invariant failure until fixed and regression-tested.
Avoid unnecessary dependencies; existing design favors Python stdlib, subprocess, Unix sockets, sqlite3, and controlled external runtimes.
Do not make claims of security properties that are not actually enforced.

frozen_invariants.D: OS containment and MCP policy are separate defenses.
frozen_invariants.E: MCP uses a Unix domain socket; no localhost TCP dependency.
frozen_invariants.F: capabilities.toml is integrity-verified, versioned, hashed, audited, and associated with a trusted expected hash; mismatch stops startup.
frozen_invariants.G: Every capability invocation follows AGY → MCP → Policy → Tool.
frozen_invariants.I: AGY cannot access audit.db, anchor.log, capabilities.toml, the trusted manifest hash, or Jarvis credentials.
frozen_invariants.J: Audit integrity includes a host-controlled external append-only anchor.
frozen_invariants.K: Any security invariant failure freezes new capability work until fixed and security tests pass.
frozen_invariants.L: Voice has zero additional authority; voice requests use the same trusted Controller/security pipeline as CLI/GUI.
frozen_invariants.M: Voice is not authentication; the MVP does not claim to authenticate the speaker.
frozen_invariants.N: Voice approvals are request-bound, fresh, and single-use. They require one exact live approval, correct session, matching canonical argument hash, unexpired state, and unconsumed state.
frozen_invariants.O: Approval recognition fails closed when approval STT confidence is below threshold. The failed attempt is rejected, does not consume or extend the approval, and does not trigger an automatic retry loop. MVP allows at most 3 failed manual confirmation attempts; the third failure denies the approval and requires re-issuing the original command.
frozen_invariants.P: AGY cannot access microphone, speaker, audio buffers, raw recordings, STT, TTS, or Voice Runtime APIs.
frozen_invariants.Q: Voice follows existing capabilities.toml classifications. SAFE executes normally; APPROVAL may use voice approval subject to G24 rules; DISABLED can never be authorized through voice.
frozen_invariants.R: Voice approval events are auditable using structured metadata including session_id, approval_id, capability, argument_hash, timestamp, STT confidence, result, expiration state, and audio_hash. Raw audio is not retained by default.
frozen_invariants.S: All user-facing output must pass through a centralized trusted Output Security Filter before CLI, TTS, GUI, notifications, or future presentation channels. It protects both tagged protected data and secrets transcribed/paraphrased by untrusted AGY.
frozen_invariants.S_addendum: Output Security Filter is trusted security infrastructure: version-controlled, integrity-verifiable, regression-tested, and fail-closed on integrity/configuration failure.

G0: 11 core security invariants represented in jarvis/security/invariants.py.
Threat model covers AGY secrets/filesystem/sandbox escape/MCP bypass, policy/tool bugs, memory poisoning, audit tampering, and sandbox regression.
G1: jarvis/sandbox/preflight.py verifies user, PID namespace, network namespace and related host capabilities.
G2: Minimal /etc, isolated /proc, minimal /dev, private /tmp, writable workspace.
Real home, SSH/GPG/config/browser credentials and private directories are unavailable.
Forbidden environment variables such as API keys/SSH tokens are stripped.
G3: Sandbox fixtures in tests/sandbox/ cover privilege escalation, network, credential harvesting and related escape attempts.
G4: Automated regression suite protects sandbox and other critical files.
G5: SecureLauncher requires preflight and explicit sandbox verification.
Structural source parsing checks for zero unsandboxed fallback paths.
No fallback to running AGY outside the sandbox.
G6: JarvisController in jarvis/core/controller.py coordinates agents, session state, policy, approval and tools.
G7: Deterministic MockAgent implemented before relying on real AGY.
Mock E2E used to verify architecture.
G8: MCP server in jarvis/mcp/server.py uses Unix domain socket only.
Jarvis acts as MCP server; AGY is the client.
G9: Corruption test appending 1 byte to capabilities.toml causes ManifestIntegrityError.
G11: Approval is cryptographically bound to exact capability plus canonical sorted-arguments JSON payload.
Supports ALLOW_ONCE, ALLOW_SESSION with expiration, DENY.
Modified capability or arguments cannot reuse approval.
G12: SQLite audit chain with cryptographic chaining.
External host-owned append-only anchor is provisioned by scripts/setup_anchor.sh.
chattr +a provides filesystem-level append-only semantics; do not describe this as absolutely immutable against host-root compromise.
JarvisController raises RuntimeError if audit logging fails instead of swallowing failures.
G13: Memory is treated as a capability.
G14: Complete MockAgent E2E exists: CLI → Jarvis → MockAgent → MCP → Policy → Tool → Audit → Response.
G15_G16: Real AGY adapter executes AGY entirely inside verified bwrap sandbox.
AGY/MCP integration uses a Unix-domain-socket bridge because AGY exposed stdio/HTTP MCP rather than direct UDS.
Host MCP socket is bind-mounted into sandbox.
AGY executable and controlled mcp config are mounted into sandbox.
mcp_bridge.py forwards stdio to fixed sandbox UDS endpoint and does not implement auth/policy.
Per-session AGY state directories are ephemeral and aggressively purged in finally blocks across success/crash/timeout/kill.
Do not make the user's real ~/.gemini writable or mount their real profile.
Preferred session structure: runtime/agy/<session-id>/config/mcp_config.json plus runtime state/logs/installation_id.
Move bridge code outside .gemini, e.g. jarvis/agent/mcp_bridge.py, and mount read-only.
G17: Read-only tools implemented: system.info, system.temperature, network.interfaces, network.status, processes.list, logs.search, files.read, files.search.
G18: Controlled mutations implemented: files.write, service.restart, package.install.
Mutation capabilities are sanitized and approval-required.

G24.summary: Voice frontend is implemented as a trusted interface around the existing Controller, policy, approval, audit, and output-security systems.
subgates: G24.3 Resource feasibility benchmark before model integration
G24.8–G24.10 Approvals, confidence, concurrent pending approvals

implementation_report.state_machine: 7 states: IDLE, LISTENING, STT, PROCESSING, WAITING_APPROVAL, EXECUTING, SPEAKING.
implementation_report.voice_session: Tracks request-bound, single-use VoicePendingApproval; enforces invariant N and 3-attempt rule from O.
implementation_report.interfaces: SpeechToText / TextToSpeech ABCs; AudioCapture / AudioPlayback ABCs; AudioChunk handles PCM, hashing, duration, WAV conversion.
implementation_report.benchmark: Hard gate passed with Vosk small + Piper on target hardware; peak RAM 484 MB; STT latency 851 ms for 3 seconds audio; report said ~4.7 GB system memory available.
implementation_report.stt: VoskSTT wrapper using vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15; lazy model loading.
implementation_report.tts: PiperTTS; TTS only streams already-filtered text to AudioPlayback.
implementation_report.runtime: VoiceRuntime captures mic input, sends bytes to STT, transitions states, immediately drops audio chunks after transcription.
implementation_report.controller: process_voice_request() uses same authorization/policy pipeline as CLI.
implementation_report.output_filter: Injected into CLI and Voice response paths.
implementation_report.approval: VoiceApprovalHandler returns PENDING for approval-required actions; confirmation.py recognizes deliberate confirmations such as 'yes jarvis confirm'.
implementation_report.confidence: Confirmation confidence threshold implemented at 0.8; low-confidence attempts rejected and count toward 3-attempt limit.
implementation_report.concurrency: Multiple pending approvals return ambiguous and require disambiguation.
implementation_report.output_security: Filter cannot be instantiated disabled; blocks SECRET/RESTRICTED tagged output; 14 regex patterns detect secrets in freeform AGY prose; violations replace entire response with generic safe string.
implementation_report.audio_privacy: GC tests verify VoiceRuntime drops audio references after STT; no disk writes in capture path; raw audio hash logged in VOICE_UTTERANCE.
implementation_report.wake: WakeEngine abstraction with MockWakeEngine and HotkeyWakeEngine; Jarvis is deaf in IDLE until triggered.
implementation_report.e2e: Read-only and mutation E2E tests completed.
implementation_report.cleanup: VoiceSession.cleanup_expired() runs synchronously at start of every voice request.

G25.purpose: Controlled automation: schedules and validated event triggers that can execute pre-authorized capability-bound jobs without creating an authorization bypass.
G25.core_rule: Automation is an independently authorized execution context. Interactive approval must never silently become standing authorization for future automated actions.

invariants.U: Automation has no implicit authorization; prior interactive approval is not standing automation permission.
invariants.V: Automation jobs are capability-bound to exact capabilities and arguments.
invariants.W: Automation cannot dynamically expand its authority, capability scope, target, arguments, privilege, schedule, or network/filesystem scope without a new authorization state.
invariants.X: Automation fails closed on invalid job definition, authorization, policy, integrity, scheduler state, sandbox, or audit state.
invariants.Y: Automation is independently auditable and every run is identifiable as automation.
invariants.Z: External triggers are untrusted input and cannot grant authority.

G25.execution_pipeline: Trigger → Job lookup → integrity/version verification → authorization verification → expiration → capability classification → Automation Policy → Jarvis Controller → AGY if needed → MCP → Tool → Audit → Output Security Filter → notification/TTS/GUI/CLI.
important_constraints: No subprocess of model-generated arbitrary command strings.
AGY may reason inside an authorized job but cannot create authorization or expand scope.
Automation scheduler must invoke Controller rather than tools directly.
Interactive approval does not create standing automation permission.
Job changes to capability/arguments/trigger/schedule/targets require a new authorization.
Use bounded concurrency and duplicate-trigger protection.
Crash recovery must not blindly replay potentially non-idempotent mutations.
Automation output uses the same Output Security Filter.

G26.focus: Multi-agent support under the same centralized policy/security system; not yet designed/implemented.

stack.wake: WakeEngine abstraction; MockWakeEngine and HotkeyWakeEngine implemented
stack.approval: Existing G11 approval infrastructure extended for voice

critical_behavior: Voice is a frontend, not a privilege boundary.
Bare 'yes' is not sufficient for voice approval; deliberate confirmation phrasing is required.
Approval confirmation is bound to a unique live approval and canonical argument hash.
Approval must be unexpired and unconsumed.
Low-confidence confirmation (<0.8 in current implementation) is rejected and counts toward a 3-failure manual retry cap.
After 3 failed manual confirmation attempts, approval is denied and original command must be re-issued.
Raw audio is ephemeral and not persisted by default.
Approval-related audio hash can be audited without storing raw audio.
All user-facing output is filtered centrally.

gui_design.status: DESIGN REQUEST READY; ACTUAL GUI IMPLEMENTATION IS A LATER G20-G22 CONCERN.
gui_design.latest_prompt_character: Condensed Stitch prompt approved by user.
visual_direction: Linux system console + modern AI workstation + mission control
gui_design.required_gui_principle: GUI is strictly a frontend. GUI → Jarvis Controller → existing security pipeline. Never GUI → Tool, Shell, AGY, systemd directly.
key_security_ux: Clearly distinguish PROPOSED → AUTHORIZED → EXECUTING → COMPLETED.
Approval UI must show capability, target, relevant arguments, reason, risk/status, expiration.
Automation UI must clearly communicate recurring authorization and expiration/revocation.
Security state must reflect real backend state: Protected, Warning, Degraded, Blocked, Unavailable.
Capability registry is informational; GUI cannot directly modify capabilities.toml/policy.
Command palette should be keyboard-friendly, e.g. Ctrl+K.

decisions_and_nonnegotiables: Do not revert to unsandboxed AGY fallback.
Do not mount the user's real ~/.gemini or credentials into AGY.
Do not replace UDS MCP with localhost TCP just for convenience.
Do not allow AGY to invoke tools outside MCP/policy.
Do not introduce a second approval/authorization system for voice, GUI, or automation.
Do not treat voice confirmation as speaker authentication.
Do not make a generic 'yes' authorize a voice mutation.
Do not store raw voice recordings by default.
Do not rely on AGY behaving honestly to protect secrets; enforce OutputSecurityFilter.
Do not remove regex/pattern secret detection because provenance tagging exists; it exists specifically to catch AGY transcription/paraphrase of secrets.
Do not let the redaction/replacement message reveal secret metadata.
Do not let interactive ALLOW_ONCE/ALLOW_SESSION silently create recurring automation permission.
Do not begin G20-G23 or G25-G26 by reordering the frozen roadmap unless the user explicitly authorizes a plan change.
